concept.name: Immediacy
concept.definition: The ability to execute a transaction promptly at or near current prices - the time dimension of market liquidity in the Sarr and Lybek (IMF, 2002) framework, and the service for which liquidity demanders compensate liquidity providers through the spread.
concept.intuition: It answers: how fast can I get this trade done right now, and what do I pay for that speed?
concept.mechanics: Reflected in execution speed for marketable orders (the SEC notes average execution speed for small marketable orders on NYSE fell from 10.1 seconds in January 2005 to 0.7 seconds in October 2009) and in the price concession - half-spread plus impact - required for immediate execution versus patient order placement.
concept.failure_modes: In fast markets immediacy can be illusory: quotes may move between order routing and execution (slippage), and during halts or fast-market conditions immediate execution may be unavailable at any displayed price.
concept.misconceptions: Immediacy is not free or guaranteed; its price is the spread plus market impact, and demanding it in size during stress can be prohibitively expensive.
concept.example: A market order in a large-cap stock executes in milliseconds at the national best offer, while the same order in a thin small-cap may take seconds and move the price.

citations.source: Sarr and Lybek, 'Measuring Liquidity in Financial Markets', IMF Working Paper WP/02/232
